name: How much debris comes out of a pool removal?

mainEntity.name: How much concrete and debris is generated when an in-ground pool is removed?
mainEntity.text: How much concrete and debris is generated when an in-ground pool is removed?

acceptedAnswer.text: The amount of debris depends on whether the project is partial or full removal and on the pool’s size and structure. Concrete pools with thick walls, heavy rebar, tile, and attached decking create far more debris than fiberglass or simpler installations. Full removals generate more haul-off because more of the shell is broken out and exported. That is why dump fees, truck access, and disposal logistics can have a big effect on the estimate. In dense Los Angeles neighborhoods, hauling can be a hidden cost if the contractor has to make multiple trips or work around narrow access. Homeowners should ask how many loads are expected, where the material goes, and whether disposal fees are included. Knowing the debris volume helps explain why one bid may be much higher than another.
acceptedAnswer.description: A pool removal can generate a large amount of concrete, rebar, tile, plumbing, and soil debris, and the volume depends on pool size and construction type. Full removal creates more haul-off than partial fill-in. Disposal access, dump fees, and the number of truckloads can strongly affect price.
